messages:
matt_sales: Kicking off — customer (ACME-Fin) wants an EU-only egress POC: BYOK, guarantee traffic never leaves EU, and full sub-processor chain for the routed path. Also asking what happens if EU capacity is full and the impact on pricing for tenant pinning vs. regular routing. Any quick guidance? :thinking:
ops_lead: Short answer: doable with tenant pinning + regional endpoint, but there are tradeoffs. We can enforce no-failover for the POC (requests will fail if local capacity exhausted). Need to surface subproc chain and BYOK constraints to customer. :warning:
priya: Tech details: runtime supports tenant_pin -> routes to configured region (e.g., eu-central-1). Default failover_policy is "prefer-local-then-failover" (cross-region to nearest healthy region). We can set failover_policy: deny-failover for POC. Caveat: deny-failover => higher chance of 503s on saturation. KV cache: no cross-region replication when BYOK is enforced (keys must stay in-region).
alex: If customer insists on never leaving EU we'll need to offer either reserved capacity in EU or accept possible downtime. I'll draft an ops checklist for certs, IP allowlists, and BYOK onboarding items. :memo:
ops_lead: Example routing snippet for our ops doc:
```yaml
routing:
  tenant_pin: eu-central-1
  failover_policy: deny-failover   # requests fail if local capacity missing
  byok: true
```
ops_lead: "deny-failover" semantics: requests return 503 with header X-RW-Failover: denied. We should warn customer in writing.
legal_jane: Subproc overview (summary): compute=AWS eu-central-1, CDN=Fastly (EU POPs), metrics=Datadog (EU), backups=S3 (EU). Need to run formal subproc attestation for EU-only flow. I'll pull the canonical subproc spreadsheet and propose DPA language for BYOK+no-failover. ETA 48h.
matt_sales: Customer also wants a ballpark cost delta for pinning+reserved capacity vs. multi-region shared capacity. They gave sample volume: ~10M tokens/month for POC.
alex: Quick back-of-envelope: tenant pinning + reserved pool in eu-central adds ~15-30% premium vs. multi-region pooling (depends on model size and run-time utilization). I'll loop in finance for a more concrete quote.
priya: Ops note: BYOK requires the KMS key to be in the same region and we do not export key material. We support AWS KMS EU keys and customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private. Onboarding checklist includes key policy granting Redwood's service principal read/encrypt permissions, and a test encrypt/decrypt handshake.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: canary tenant-pin policy applied to staging-eu at 1792468200 :rocket:
ops_lead: If customer wants HSM on-prem for key material, that's an enterprise-only flow; timescales + pricing differ. Also monitoring telemetry: we can route telemetry to EU Datadog but some infra-level telemetry (host metrics) may hit provider endpoints — will list specifics in the attestation.
legal_jane: Also flag: some sub-processors have EU POPs but contractual processing may still have cross-border clauses. We'll mark each vendor row with "data residency risk" and recommended mitigations.
matt_sales: Action items: alex -> ops checklist + initial cost estimate, priya -> KV cache/fallback doc + short FAQ for the customer, legal_jane -> subproc spreadsheet + DPA snippet, ops_lead -> confirm whether infra team can allow "deny-failover" for a short POC window. I'll update ACME-Fin after we have the doc + numbers. :thumbsup:
alex: I'll aim to share the ops checklist and a sample cost calc by EOD tomorrow.
priya: I'll add a short section on expected failure modes (503 scenarios) and a recommended testing script. Example test: `curl -H "x-tenant: acme-fin" https://api.redwood.ai/generate` expecting 503 + X-RW-Failover: denied when simulated load hits saturation.
matt_sales: Ping — any update on the subproc sheet? :eyes:
